metallic.types: Hematite (Fe 60–70%, red ore, 85% of Indian reserves) & Magnetite (Fe 72%, black magnetic ore, 15%)
metallic.rank: India is the 4th largest producer in the world (after Australia, Brazil, China)
metallic.leadingState: Odisha (produces >50% of national total), followed by Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Jharkhand

majorBelts.name: Odisha-Jharkhand Belt
majorBelts.mines: Badampahar, Gorumahisani, Sulaipat (Mayurbhanj); Joda, Barbil, Thakurani (Kendujhar); Noamundi and Gua (Singhbhum, Jharkhand)
majorBelts.feeds: Steel plants at Jamshedpur (Tata), Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur, Burnpur

majorBelts.name: Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur Belt
majorBelts.mines: Bailadila Range (Bastar, Chhattisgarh — super high-grade hematite deposits); Dalli-Rajhara (Durg)
majorBelts.feeds: Bhilai Steel Plant; exported as high-grade lumps to Japan and South Korea via Visakhapatnam Port

majorBelts.name: Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru Belt
majorBelts.mines: Sandur, Hospet (Ballari); Kudremukh (100% export-oriented magnetite, ore transported as liquid slurry via 67 km pipeline to Panambur/Mangaluru port); Bababudan Hills

majorBelts.name: Maharashtra-Goa Belt
majorBelts.mines: Ratnagiri (Maharashtra); Bicholim, Sanquelim (Goa — low-grade ore exported via Marmagao Port)

metallic.types: Pyrolusite and Psilomelane ores; essential ferro-alloy input (approx. 10 kg manganese required to manufacture 1 tonne of steel)
metallic.rank: India holds significant reserves, mostly in ancient Dharwar rock systems
metallic.leadingState: Odisha (Bonai, Kendujhar, Sundargarh), followed by Madhya Pradesh (Balaghat, Chhindwara), Maharashtra (Nagpur, Bhandara), Karnataka
majorBelts: Nagpur-Bhandara-Balaghat belt holds the highest quality metallurgical grade ore in India (MOIL headquarters at Nagpur)

metallic.types: Hydrated aluminium oxide formed by intense weathering of laterite rocks on plateau summits
metallic.rank: India is self-sufficient and exports alumina; smelting requires huge electricity (~14,000 kWh per tonne), so smelters site near cheap hydro/thermal power

majorBelts.name: Panchpatmali & Baphlimali Deposits (Koraput & Rayagada, Odisha)
majorBelts.desc: Largest bauxite reserve in India; feeds NALCO refinery at Damanjodi and smelter at Angul; Vedanta at Lanjigarh

majorBelts.name: Amarkantak Plateau & Maikal Hills (MP/Chhattisgarh)
majorBelts.desc: Feeds HINDALCO smelter at Renukoot (UP) powered by Rihand Dam

metallic.types: Chalcopyrite ore; India is critically deficient in copper, importing over 85% of copper concentrates
metallic.leadingState: Madhya Pradesh (Balaghat - Malanjkhand copper deposit produces ~50% of Indian ore), followed by Rajasthan (Khetri-Singhana belt, Jhunjhunu), Jharkhand (Singhbhum - Mosabani/Rakha)
majorBelts: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL, PSU) operates Malanjkhand and Khetri mines

nonMetallic.properties: Exceptional dielectric strength, low power-loss factor, insulating, high heat resistance; critical for electrical and electronic equipment
nonMetallic.leadingState: Jharkhand (Koderma belt — historically 'Mica Capital of the World'), followed by Andhra Pradesh (Nellore belt) and Rajasthan (Bhilwara-Ajmer belt)
nonMetallic.status: India was historically the world's top exporter of sheet mica; synthetic substitutes and glass fibre have reduced global demand.

nonMetallic.properties: Calcium carbonate sedimentary rock; primary raw material for the cement industry and flux material in blast furnaces
nonMetallic.leadingState: Rajasthan (Chittorgarh, Nagaur), Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat
nonMetallic.status: Cement plants cluster along limestone belts (e.g., Satna-Katni belt in MP, Chittorgarh in Rajasthan).

fossilFuels.types: Anthracite (hard, >85% C, found only in J&K/Kalakot); Bituminous (commercial, 60–80% C, non-coking & coking); Lignite (brown coal, 40–55% C); Peat (<40% C)
fossilFuels.geology: Two distinct geological ages: (1) Gondwana Coal Fields (~250 Ma, Permian, accounts for 98% of reserves and production, low sulphur, high ash content 20–40%); (2) Tertiary Coal Fields (~55 Ma, Eocene, accounts for 2%, high sulphur content, found in Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal, Nagaland).
fossilFuels.leadingState: Jharkhand ranks 1st in reserves (Jharia, Bokaro, Dhanbad, Karanpura), followed by Odisha (Talcher, Ib Valley), Chhattisgarh (Korba, Hasdeo Arand), West Bengal (Raniganj — oldest coalfield in India, 1774).
fossilFuels.ligniteReserves: Neyveli in Tamil Nadu holds over 70% of India's lignite reserves, mined by NLC India for pithead thermal power generation; also in Palana (Rajasthan) and Gujarat.

basins.name: Offshore Western Basin (Bombay High & Bassein)
basins.desc: Discovered 1974 by ONGC drilling ship 'Sagar Samrat', located 160 km west of Mumbai in the Arabian Sea continental shelf.

basins.name: Assam / Brahmaputra Shelf Basin
basins.desc: Digboi (oldest operational refinery in Asia, 1901), Naharkatiya, Moran-Hugrijan, Sibsagar; oil piped to Barauni and Guwahati refineries.

basins.name: Gujarat / Cambay Basin
basins.desc: Ankleshwar, Kalol, Mehsana, Gandhar, Nawagam, and offshore Aliabet island.

basins.name: Rajasthan / Barmer-Sanchore Basin
basins.share: Largest onshore oil discovery in recent decades
basins.desc: Mangala, Bhagyam, and Aishwarya fields operated by Cairn/Vedanta, producing ~20% of domestic crude.

basins.name: Krishna-Godavari (KG) Offshore Deepwater Basin
basins.desc: Deepwater blocks KG-D6 (Reliance-BP) and KG-DWN-98/2 (ONGC) producing natural gas from deep sea wells.

criticalMinerals.overview: In 2023, the Ministry of Mines identified 30 critical minerals essential for economic development and national security, focusing on electric vehicles, batteries, semiconductors, and defence.
criticalMinerals.ncmaMission: National Critical Minerals Mission (NCMM) approved in January 2025 with an outlay of ₹34,300 crore to secure supply chains, boost GSI exploration (1,200 projects), and establish domestic refining/recycling.
keyFinds: Lithium: Inferred resources of 5.9 million tonnes identified in Salal-Haimana area, Reasi district, Jammu & Kashmir (2023); lithium pegmatite reserves in Mandya, Karnataka.
Rare Earth Elements (REEs): Monazite beach sand deposits in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra, and Odisha containing cerium, neodymium, lanthanum managed by IREL (India) Ltd.
Overseas Acquisition: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd. (KABIL — JV of NALCO, HCL, MECL) acquired 5 lithium brine blocks in Catamarca Province, Argentina (2024).

nuclearMinerals.mines: Jaduguda, Bhatin, Narwapahar, Turamdih (Singhbhum copper belt, Jharkhand operated by UCIL); Tummalapalle (Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh — world-class low-grade uranium deposit in Cuddapah basin); Domiasiat/Kylleng-Pyndengsohiong (Meghalaya).

nuclearMinerals.reserves: India holds the world's largest known reserves of Thorium, contained in the mineral Monazite in coastal placer beach sands of Kerala (Chavara), Tamil Nadu (Manavalakurichi), Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha.
nuclearMinerals.strategy: Foundation of Stage 3 of India's Three-Stage Nuclear Power Programme (Dr. Homi Bhabha) using Advanced Heavy Water Reactors (AHWR) and Fast Breeder Reactors (PFBR at Kalpakkam).
